entityName: Dr. Bratzel Center of Automotive Management GmbH & Co. KG
entityDescription:
The Center of Automotive Management (CAM) was founded by Prof. Stefan Bratzel in 2004 with the support of the University of Applied Sciences of Bergisch Gladbach. Its function is to serve as a partner for car manufacturers, suppliers and retailers concerning market research and strategic consultancy. Currently the CAM consists of a regular staff of five team members and is located in the town of Bergisch Gladbach near Cologne. 
Shortly after its foundation the CAM established two separate approaches to analyse and determine the competitiveness of the global automotive industry. The first approach was the establishment of an innovation database. Since 2005 the CAM systematically gathered more than 20.000 product and technological innovations of 40 global car manufacturers and their 100 brands. Sources of information are, amongst others, journals, press releases and on-site surveys on international automobile exhibitions. CAM only accepts identified technological improvements as „innovation“ if they meet three conditions: Innovations must have a perceptible benefit for customers (compared to the status quo), they must be appropriately presented, so that a broad public could take notice of it and they must be available as products, at least as prototypes. If the innovation matches this criteria it is then systematically categorized in seven main technology fields and currently more than 700 innovation types. Finally each innovation is then individually assessed using four different criteria which are its innovation level, originality, maturity level and customer benefit.
Together with our annual patent analysis of the automotive industry this approach allows us to determine the innovation landscape of the industry and to forecast its technological development on a mid- and long-term range perspective. As the database also provides insights in the innovation performance and priorities of each manufacturer it can also be used as a tool for competitive analyses and is therefore licensed by a couple of notable OEMs. 
The other approach focuses on the market and financial performance of the industry competitors. The CAM has established a performance database which contains the sales, financial and other performance figures of each car manufacturer since back in 2002 and is updated quarterly. The financial figures are derived from the official financial statements and include performance indicators like R&D expenditures, EBIT and operative cash flow. The market figures contain information about the global and regional performance (e.g. Europe, NAFTA, BRICs) and are gathered from official statements and reports from manufactures, governmental bodies and advocacy groups. 
Both approaches are used as an empirical foundation for in-depth studies and projects for manufacturers, suppliers as well as governmental and non-governmental organisations. The results of both approaches are also used to provide an annual study about the performance of the industry’s competitors by aligning the innovation, market and financial success of each competitor, resulting in a ranking of the competitors by applying our ‘Automotive Performance Index’ (API) scheme. This approach allows us not only to identify the high, medium and low performers of the competition, but also to provide reliable empirical evidence for the results and statements.

description:
Mapular provides progressive location data solutions across the globe. We support organisations and businesses to harness their data, extract its value and turn it into an asset.
Using our geospatial skills, we design and build tools to transform underutilised data into an asset. Wherever your data is sourced from - satellites, planes, drones, field collection, IoT, third parties, or through integration with your other business systems - we can help you gain near real-time visibility of your operations. Today that includes AI systems for geospatial data: MCP-based tool servers, geospatial embeddings and data pipelines, and bespoke Esri/ArcGIS development (Esri partner, Nonprofit Specialty).
Orbica UG launched in February 2017 (renamed Mapular UG in 2023) out of a desire that has grown into our purpose: "To enhance billions of lives through the power of geography." Headquartered in Berlin, we have collaborated with many medium and large enterprises across Germany, New Zealand and Australia. Delivered work includes UNESCO's World Heritage monitoring platform, now an Esri case study, and a forest-carbon MRV platform for carbon markets.
We have a highly experienced team, with expertise in remote sensing, Earth observation, geospatial analysis and development, full-stack development, AI and data science, agile and collaborative delivery, and a full suite of business analysis skills. The team's combined knowledge makes Mapular unique in its ability to deliver innovative, complex and specific solutions for tough problems. Thinking outside of the square is what we do every day.

entityDescription:
Satlantis France SAS is an independent company, legally distinct from Satlantis Microsat (Spain), although both entities share a common technological heritage and vision. Operating autonomously, Satlantis France defines its own R&D agenda, strategic roadmap, and industrial partnerships, with a core focus on high-resolution polarimetric imaging and advanced Earth observation solutions for both civil and defense applications.
As the group’s center of excellence for optical polarimetry, Satlantis France develops innovative payloads that integrate compact, high-performance sensors, onboard image processing, and AI-driven analytics. Our current developments focus on generating fused imagery that combines polarimetry, multispectral data, and very high spatial resolution, enabling the detection of subtle spectral and directional features in complex or obscured environments.
Key application domains under investigation include:– Methane detection with advanced atmospheric discrimination,– Monitoring of microplastics in marine environments,– Air quality assessment,– Detection of camouflaged or concealed structures,– High-resolution environmental surveillance.
In parallel, Satlantis France contributes to the group’s near real-time satellite video capability, delivering native resolutions enhanced through proprietary algorithms to achieve effective ground resolutions of approximately 1 meter. This functionality enables dynamic monitoring of rapidly evolving scenarios, including:– Convoy tracking and route surveillance,– Observation of active conflict zones,– Wave pattern analysis for coastal monitoring and bathymetry,– Fast-response disaster impact assessment.
Our mission is to transform satellite data into actionable geospatial intelligence, tailored to the operational needs of space agencies, public authorities, and industrial stakeholders.
Through these capabilities, Satlantis France contributes to Europe’s strategic autonomy in space-based technologies, offering a unique polarimetric and video imaging solution deployable on agile LEO platforms and scalable to constellation architectures. We actively participate in European collaborative initiatives and welcome scientific and institutional partnerships to bring this critical capability into operational service.

entityDescription:
Retree&Space Solutions SL es una empresa dedicada a la regeneración de ecosistemas degradados mediante la reforestación con especies autóctonas. Su misión combina la restauración ambiental con un impacto económico y social.
Qué hace:
- Crea sumideros de carbono rastreables mediante la plantación de especies autóctonas que regeneran los suelos, fortalecen la biodiversidad y apoyan las economías rurales.
- Adopta una postura explícita en contra del ecoblanqueo, ofreciendo mediciones de absorción de CO2 trazables en lugar de meras declaraciones de intenciones.
- Integra la tecnología satelital y la observación de la Tierra para monitorear y verificar el progreso de la reforestación a lo largo del tiempo, sin depender únicamente de la verificación sobre el terreno.
Dos ofertas principales:
- El servicio de reforestación regenerativa es el núcleo del negocio y está dirigido a empresas que buscan medir y verificar su absorción de CO2 a través de proyectos de impacto demostrable.
- Carbin es la herramienta de trazabilidad del carbono de Retree&Space Solutions SL (actualmente en desarrollo): combina datos satelitales con monitoreo sobre el terreno para verificar y rastrear continuamente el carbono capturado y la salud de los ecosistemas restaurados.
Público objetivo: Empresas que buscan una medición verificable y trazable de la absorción de CO2, no una simple declaración de intenciones.

- Facilitating meetings and organizing conferences, workshops and symposia

entityDescription:
Cerberus Nuclear was created to approach technical consultancy with an emphasis on creativity and innovation. We bring together highly specialist skills and industry-wide experience to offer comprehensive Radiation Shielding, Criticality Safety, Nuclear Characterisation, Data Science and Software Development services for Nuclear, Medical, Research, Defence, Fusion and Space sectors.
Radiation Shielding 
Our highly experienced team provide radiation shielding design, dose assessment and peer review services covering the full project design life-cycle. We utilise the latest calculation methods combined with high-power computing to efficiently deliver accurate and reliable results. Our team are skilled in communicating complex data to stakeholders and regulatory bodies. 
Criticality Safety 
Cerberus Nuclear has the largest independent criticality safety team in the UK and has significant experience supporting key clients across the nuclear industry. We provide support across the full nuclear fuel cycle and offer a complete range of criticality services, including working on the behalf of regulators within the UK and internationally. 
Nuclear Innovation
Cerberus Nuclear have produced high-level strategies for characterisation of high-profile nuclear facilities. Using our established expertise in nuclear data science we utilise the latest developments in machine learning and computer vision to develop new innovative techniques to support on-site characterisation and data analysis.

Space Applications

With Cerberus Nuclear looking to utilise its nuclear heritage in the space sector, we are already able to handle the complete process required to find the actual radiation exposure a spacecraft and its components experience in a given orbit using Monte Carlo radiation transport codes. This covers the radiation shielding impacts of the outer structure of the spacecraft as well as its internal geometry, and can be completed to ECSS standards. Our current capabilities include:
- Radiation Mission Environment Specification
- Total Ionising Dose (TID) Assessment
- Total Non-Ionising Dose (TNID) Assessment
- Single Event Effects (SEE) Assessment
- Bulk Shielding Analysis
- Component and Material Radiation Threat Analysis

Cerberus Nuclear has the largest independent criticality safety team in the UK and has significant experience supporting key clients across the nuclear industry. We provide support across the full nuclear fuel cycle and offer a complete range of criticality services, including working on the behalf of regulators within the UK and internationally. 
Nuclear Innovation
Cerberus Nuclear have produced high-level strategies for characterisation of high-profile nuclear facilities. Using our established expertise in nuclear data science we utilise the latest developments in machine learning and computer vision to develop new innovative techniques to support on-site characterisation and data analysis.

Space Applications

With Cerberus Nuclear looking to utilise its nuclear heritage in the space sector, we are already able to handle the complete process required to find the actual radiation exposure a spacecraft and its components experience in a given orbit using Monte Carlo radiation transport codes. This covers the radiation shielding impacts of the outer structure of the spacecraft as well as its internal geometry, and can be completed to ECSS standards. Our current capabilities include:
- Radiation Mission Environment Specification
- Total Ionising Dose (TID) Assessment
- Total Non-Ionising Dose (TNID) Assessment
- Single Event Effects (SEE) Assessment
- Bulk Shielding Analysis
- Component and Material Radiation Threat Analysis

entityName: ZORA Reentry Systems s. r. o.
entityDescription: ZORA Reentry Technologies is an early-stage Slovak deep-tech company developing advanced thermal protection systems (TPS) for spacecraft re-entry applications. Founded by four engineers with hands-on experience from the HARTS heatshield project, ZORA is commercializing a 3D-woven, carbon-fiber thermal protection material designed to compete with established high-performance ablative solutions such as PICA, while offering superior geometric adaptability and material configurability. The company addresses a clear gap in the European space market: the lack of accessible, configurable TPS materials that can be tailored to different mission envelopes without costly full redesigns. ZORA's material platform enables controlled variation of density, weave architecture, and thickness, allowing integration into non-standard geometries for re-entry vehicles, payload return capsules, and high-temperature aerothermal components. Currently at TRL 2–3, ZORA is targeting TRL 4–5 by the end of its ESA BIC Slovakia incubation period (2026–2028), with a focus on repeatable in-house manufacturing, standardized characterization datasets, and first customer evaluation samples. The company targets European institutional space programmes and commercial re-entry startups, with a longer-term roadmap extending into reusable thermal protection architectures and non-space high-temperature industrial applications.

entityDescription: GUIDE is a GNSS testing laboratory accredited in Geolocation. It is specialized in the performance characterization of positioning systems inland environments where GNSS measurements are highly distorted. Two test methodologies are implemented. One, to assess their "typical" performance relative to the usual accuracy/precision according to areas and the other, for their performance in "critical" situations where the integrity of the measurements must remain under control. In the first case, GUIDE digitizes real GNSS signals and then replays them on test benches many times. These iterations have the advantage of • increase the number of measurement samples for a better characterization of uncertainties. • reveal local constraints of test scenarios impacting the positioning measurements. In the second case, GUIDE uses tools of simulations of last generation to reconstruct the conditions of propagation within synthetic environments representative of the reality (Bridge, Buildings, Foliage, ...). These typical virtual scenes, modeled in 3D, are used to simulate the reception conditions of GNSS signals. The local biases are rendered in the first stratum of scenario which can be enriched with the second stratum to add Global "feared events", such as those from satellites or high layers of the atmosphere, ie. especially the ionosphere. Different types of interferences (domestic, industrial or intentional ones) can be mixed with all these GNSS signals to assess the resilience level of positioning systems.

In the first case, GUIDE digitizes real GNSS signals and then replays them on test benches many times. These iterations have the advantage of • increase the number of measurement samples for a better characterization of uncertainties. • reveal local constraints of test scenarios impacting the positioning measurements. In the second case, GUIDE uses tools of simulations of last generation to reconstruct the conditions of propagation within synthetic environments representative of the reality (Bridge, Buildings, Foliage, ...). These typical virtual scenes, modeled in 3D, are used to simulate the reception conditions of GNSS signals. The local biases are rendered in the first stratum of scenario which can be enriched with the second stratum to add Global "feared events", such as those from satellites or high layers of the atmosphere, ie. especially the ionosphere. Different types of interferences (domestic, industrial or intentional ones) can be mixed with all these GNSS signals to assess the resilience level of positioning systems.

description:
Tuxera is defining the physical AI data layer: the software that ensures data integrity, reliability, and performance in systems where AI operates in the physical world. From autonomous vehicles and industrial robots to smart energy grids and aerospace platforms, physical AI systems depend on data they can trust, captured at the edge and delivered at scale to the data center. 
Tuxera provides that layer: embedded file systems and flash management that protect data at the point of capture, safety-certified networking that moves it securely, and the Fusion platform that delivers enterprise-grade, multi-protocol file sharing for AI training pipelines and high-performance workloads. 
With nearly 20 years of engineering heritage and software running in more than 500 million devices worldwide, Tuxera is the data layer that physical AI is built on, from edge to data center.

entityDescription: The professorship conducts research in the space geodetic techniques Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS), Satellite Laser Ranging (SLR), Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI), and Doppler Orbitography and Radiopositioning Integrated by Satellite (DORIS) as well as their combination to so-called global terrestrial reference frames. The reference frames are the metrological basis of almost all geodetic observations. Highly accurate and long-term stable reference frames are essential for the observation and monitoring of the Earth’s system.
